chunk_findings.detail: The new test does not model two give-ups of one waiter, and its assertion cannot pass on a correct park-on-retry implementation. Inside the holder, round 0 times `patient` out, then starts a blocking `_waiter` named `patient` and waits until that ticket is queued. Round 1 then calls `SL.hold(..., "patient")` again while that waiter is still queued, starts `late1`, and starts a second blocking `_waiter` also named `patient`. Four acquirers are joined (`late0`, `patient`, `late1`, `patient`). After the holder releases, a correct queue yields `["patient", "late0", "late1", "patient"]` (the first parked retry runs, then the two lates, then the extra same-name waiter), which fails `assert order == ["patient", "late0", "late1"]`. The second short `hold` is a concurrent same-name acquisition, not a retry after the first waiter has left the queue, so the “gives up twice and keeps the same place both times” claim is never exercised. The unfixed code also fails the assertion (four names, patient not stably first), so the test does not go red-then-green on B5225d3ad22.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite still does not lock B5225d3ad22's "twice in a row" loss of place. Both `SL.hold(..., "patient")` calls run while the queue has no other waiter, and the loop's `any(... .parked and "patient" in p.name)` is not cleared between iterations. After the first timeout leaves `queue/*patient*.parked`, the second `hold` can raise `SuiteBusy` without parking (or can drop that ticket) and the same leftover file still satisfies the assert. `late` is started only after both give-ups, so a single leftover park reclaimed by the final `_waiter("patient")` still yields `order == ["patient", "late"]`. A regression that parks once and loses the place on the second give-up — the reported starvation — passes this test.

data.probe: round 1 reuse: _Ticket.__init__ renaming the round-0 .parked back to .ticket happens BEFORE round-1's hold loop, so round-0's parked file cannot satisfy round-1's assert; a .parked exists after round 1 only if round-1's give-up parked it fresh (__exit__ self.park rename). Against the code at the bug's filing there is no .parked mechanism at all, so glob('*.parked') is empty and the round-0 assert fails already. And even a hypothetical 'parks once, drops the second' code fails round-1's assert, since the round-1 __init__ consumed the one parked file. The test is red on unfixed, green on fixed.
